frequency_question: How often do structural frictions (committee delays, holds, lack of floor time) successfully prevent confirmation before the deadline when time is short?
membership_rule: Includes all executive nominees facing organized Senate opposition or procedural delays with fewer than 45 days remaining in a legislative session. Excludes uncontroverted routine promotions.
provenance_note: 8 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 10 named instances of high friction under tight legislative timelines; 8 resulted in failure to confirm.
known_gaps: Some voice-vote or non-controversial accelerations are excluded by definition since they lack structural friction.
multiplier: 8 hits out of 10 total identified contentious late-session/short-window nominations
validity_reason: Tied to the procedural rules of the U.S. Senate, which change slowly but reset partially with each new Congress.
